answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil identities by requiring each new account to escrow a stake and earn access through repeated, randomly assigned trades with established agents. Counterparties attest only after successful delivery, while cryptographic records make conflicting behavior provable; a detected fake identity loses its stake and reputation. Creating thousands of accounts therefore requires capital and time, and splitting activity across identities cannot cheaply manufacture trust. A cedar seller may tell a fable in the garden, but each claim must survive costly interaction.
